title_as_printed: Experimental Isopiestic Molalities (Reference and Ternary Solutions), Calculated Water Activities, and Temperatures for Various LiCl Salt Mole Ratios
pressure_note: not stated (isopiestic equilibrium at the vapour pressure of the solutions; no pressure reported)

value.what: total molality of the LiCl + MgCl2 mixture (both salts together) in isopiestic equilibrium with the MgCl2 reference

value2.what: isopiestic molality of the MgCl2 reference solution

aw.what: water activity of the reference MgCl2 solution at its molality, calculated by the authors from the Valyashko et al. Pitzer parameter compilation

composition.other_species: ternary LiCl-MgCl2-H2O; composition given as salt mole fraction y_LiCl = n_LiCl/(n_MgCl2+n_LiCl), set per block by the label rows; total molality is the value column. LiCl is outside the six-ion set, MgCl2 is in scope.

conversion_needs: molality of each salt = m(Total) x y_LiCl (LiCl) and m(Total) x (1 - y_LiCl) (MgCl2), if m(Total) is the sum of both salt molalities (inferred from Eq. 1; the text does not define m(Total) explicitly)
notes: Printed layout is wide (one m(Total) column per y_LiCl 0.1-0.7, one row per isopiestic run, dash for no measurement). STACKED here: one label row per y_LiCl block, rows in the printed run order, cells printed as '-' omitted (no measurement). aw and T are repeated for each run in each block. The printed table has no y_LiCl = 0.8 column although the text says 0.8 was measured and then excluded because the mixture composition was evidently wrong. Two printed values look inconsistent with the monotone trend and are kept as printed: y=0.6 at aw 0.48003 is 6.9878 (neighbours 8.0792, 7.9261) and y=0.6 at aw 0.56503 is 5.2812 (neighbour run at 0.54658 is 6.7333); the authors say nothing about them. Printed T values scatter 428.25-428.76 K (nominal 155.5 C).
quality_remarks: audit 2026-10-02: The two odd y=0.6 values (6.9878 at reference 5.5882; 5.2812 at reference 4.8531) are also 18-22 percent below the Zdanovskii-Stokes-Robinson estimate from the LiCl binary at the same reference molalities, so they are probable misprints; a third value (6.7333 at reference 5.0110) is about 4 percent low. Kept as printed; flag as low quality if ever used.
